ACTION: Read `~/.claude/skills/subagent-driven-development/references/fix-loop.md` again. It sets who fixes round 5 (resumed or fresh), how the re-review runs, and the adjudication rules.

ACTION: Dispatch the round 5 fix subagent with model `fable`. The prompt gives the Task 6 brief file from `scripts/task-brief`, the review finding F1 verbatim, and the paths to the round 4 fix report and the diff file. It asks the subagent to first write a failing test that starts the refresh thread and shows the race at `cache/refresh.py:88`, then fix the root cause, then run the covering tests and report their output. It carries the Global Constraints block verbatim and no history from earlier tasks.

ACTION: When the fix report arrives, build a new review package with `scripts/review-package` and dispatch the scoped re-review from `re-review-prompt.md` at model `opus`, because this is a subtle concurrency change.

Task 6 is still open on one Important finding, F1. The round 4 lock did not fix the race at `cache/refresh.py:88`. Its test passed only because it never started the refresh thread. Round 4 was a thorough attempt by `opus`, so I am moving round 5 up to `fable`. Round 5 is the last fix attempt before I adjudicate what is still open. I will not mark Task 6 complete until the re-review is clean.

`★ Insight ─────────────────────────────────────`
- A concurrency test that never starts the competing thread proves nothing. It passes whether or not the race exists.
- Asking for a failing test first makes the fix prove itself. The test must fail on the old code and pass on the new code.
`─────────────────────────────────────────────────`
